findings.detail: The prose rule 'an order in scope whose customer_id names a customer absent from customers contributes to no output row' is never guaranteed by any graded population condition. Walking each: development — 'Tiny C1/C2 debug data: exactly two customers', 'Every customer has at least one completed order', 'No NULL customer_id, no duplicate rows' — no dangling customer_id stated (and development is not a grading discriminator anyway). primary — lists cancelled orders, customers with no orders, customers with orders but no completed orders, and 'Some COMPLETED orders have NULL customer_id and carry item lines' — NULL is mentioned explicitly but a DANGLING (non-existent customer) customer_id is not stated to be present. resampled — 'Same generator and conditions as primary', hence the same gap. counterfactual — 'Literal constructed rows only — exactly the C10/C11/C12 case', with C10 (customer with no orders), C11 (one completed order, 3 items = 45), C12 (only cancelled order) — no dangling-customer order. stress — skewed customer, duplicate headers, duplicate item lines, ties, 'Every customer has at least one completed order' — no dangling customer_id stated. Consequence: a solver that FULL/RIGHT-joins orders to customers, or that unions in order-side keys (e.g. builds the customer key set from orders instead of customers, or aggregates orders by customer_id and left-joins customers onto that), would emit an extra output row keyed by a nonexistent customer_id and still match gold everywhere, because no population is stated to contain such an order. Note the corresponding NULL case IS covered by primary/resampled, so only the dangling variant is blind.

proposed_case.params: {"variant": "customer_key_set_from_orders", "description": "build the output key set as the union of customers.customer_id and the non-null customer_id values of completed orders (right/full outer join instead of driving strictly from customers), keeping all other logic correct: dedupe (order_id, customer_id) headers, sum quantity*unit_price per order, COALESCE measures to 0, sort by customer_id"}
proposed_case.rationale: No stated condition in development, primary, resampled, counterfactual or stress guarantees a completed order whose customer_id is present but absent from customers; the NULL case is explicitly excluded from the key set by the variant itself (only non-null customer_id values are unioned), so primary/resampled's NULL-customer orders do not catch it. Every graded population therefore FAILS to distinguish this wrong logic — which is why this is reported as a population blindness; the case is expected to keep full reward everywhere and should be treated as evidence for adding dangling-customer_id rows to primary/resampled or counterfactual rather than as a promotable gate case.

findings.summary: No graded population is stated to contain a completed order whose customer_id names a customer absent from customers, so an inner-join-only-on-orders variant (or, more precisely, dropping the dangling-order exclusion) plus other dangling-key mishandling cannot be distinguished.

findings.detail: The prose rule 'an order in scope whose customer_id names a customer absent from customers contributes to no output row, because the output has a row only for customers that exist in customers' is not guaranteed by any graded population condition. Full sweep: development \u2014 'Tiny C1/C2 debug data: exactly two customers', 'Every customer has at least one completed order', 'No NULL customer_id, no duplicate rows' \u2014 no dangling customer_id stated. primary \u2014 conditions name cancelled orders, customers with no orders, customers with orders but no completed orders, 'Some COMPLETED orders have NULL customer_id and carry item lines', and multi-item completed orders; a DANGLING (non-existent) customer_id is never stated. resampled \u2014 'Same generator and conditions as primary; new seed and new id ranges', hence the identical gap. counterfactual \u2014 'Literal constructed rows only \u2014 exactly the C10/C11/C12 case': C10 customer with no orders, C11 one completed order with 3 items totalling 45, C12 only a cancelled order worth 100 \u2014 no dangling-customer order. stress \u2014 skewed customer, exact-duplicate headers, exact-duplicate item lines, ties, 'Every customer has at least one completed order' \u2014 no dangling customer_id stated. Consequence: a solver that derives the customer key set as the union of customers.customer_id with the non-null customer_id values of completed orders (RIGHT/FULL join, or aggregating orders first and left-joining customers onto that) would emit spurious rows keyed by nonexistent customers, yet match the frozen gold on every graded population. The NULL-customer_id half of the rule IS covered by primary/resampled; only the dangling half is blind. Repair: add at least one completed order with a customer_id absent from customers to primary/resampled's generator conditions, or a C13 literal row to counterfactual.
findings.summary: No graded population is stated to contain a completed order whose customer_id names a customer absent from customers, so a solver that builds the output key set from orders instead of strictly from customers is indistinguishable everywhere.
